inputs.share_count_basis: 457,439,185 shares issued less 1,305,694 treasury shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 Tanshin, after the 5,000,000-share cancellation of 27 Feb 2026) = 456.13m, plus ~0.44m dilutive stock-option shares per the FY2025 diluted-EPS note (FY2025 AR line 11294) = 456.6m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks (Y20.1bn FY2025, Y5.7bn H1 FY2026, Y10bn FY2026 limit) fund the flat count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, consolidated cash-flow statement share-based payment add-back (Y1,733mn); Japanese restricted-stock plan, no separate equity-award tax line disclosed. SBC is 0.18% of revenue and immaterial.
inputs.price_note: Yahoo Finance chart API regular Tokyo close; 52-week range 3043-6890. Not an after-hours print. The stock has fallen ~45% since early August 2026 on a steady weekly slide (weekly closes 5,860 -> 3,198), so the price is live, not frozen.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 balance sheet (H1 FY2026 Tanshin): bonds, borrowings and lease liabilities Y88,382mn current + Y139,913mn non-current = Y228,295mn, less cash Y153,023mn. The interim does not split lease liabilities out; FY2025 lease liabilities were Y23,386mn (FY2025 AR line 10310) against Y201,350mn of bonds and borrowings, and are assumed flat at ~Y23,386mn, giving ex-lease debt of ~Y204,909mn. Net debt ex-lease = Y51,877mn. Lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (see lease_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10-year JGB ~1.7-1.8% (Nov 2026), ERP 6.0%, beta ~1.25 for a semicap-exposed Japanese industrial -> cost of equity ~9.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.0% (FY2025 average borrowing rate 0.9-2.5%); D/(D+E) ~20% at the 0.44x reported D/E -> WACC ~7.6%, rounded UP to 8.0% to sit between the house 9% keiretsu-supplier reference and a pure large-cap JPY industrial. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full IFRS 16 lease cash cost -- principal Y6,523mn (financing) + interest Y419mn (operating) = Y6,942mn, 0.72% of FY2025 revenue -- is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (Y23,386mn) are excluded from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is therefore ex right-of-use depreciation: Y34,804mn total less Y5,823mn ROU depreciation = Y28,981mn, 3.0% of revenue (FY2025 AR lines 8620, 10005, 10009, 8662).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Non-controlling interests (Y11,848mn stock at 30 June 2026) took Y2,959mn of FY2025 profit, 2.6% of operating profit. That leakage is folded into cash_tax_rate_path: 28.8% cash tax (Y32,730mn paid / Y113,802mn OP) + 2.6% NCI share = 31.5% combined. Calibration: FY2025 OP Y113,802mn x (1 - 0.315) = Y77,954mn vs reported attributable profit Y76,633mn -- ties within net finance cost. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received Y1,891mn (FY2025) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt positive ex-lease (Y51.9bn) so there is no cash pile being double counted, and the component build starts from operating EBITDA, which excludes finance income anyway. Set to 0 per the method's materiality rule.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2: non-US cyclical industrial, with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied -- JPY WACC, single lease treatment (B), NCI folded into the tax/leakage rate, matching-asset bridge for equity instruments, SBC kept visible at 0.18%). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end; FY changed from March to December in 2017, the FY2017-9mo stub is excluded from all CAGRs). JGAAP FY2015-FY2020, IFRS FY2021 onward. 5-for-1 split July 2024; all share data post-split. CRITICAL BASE-YEAR CAVEAT: FY2025 reported FCF is -Y51.5bn because capex nearly doubled to Y92.2bn (9.6% of revenue vs a FY2021-24 average of 4.5%) and working capital absorbed ~Y70bn (deferred revenue fell Y26bn). The base case does NOT carry that forward: capex is modelled at 8.0% in FY2026 (H1 FY2026 run-rate Y41.8bn) normalising to 4.2% by FY2033, and the FCF margin is rebuilt from components (EBITDA 15.7% -> 16.5%). A semicap digestion year (0% growth, -1pp margin) is embedded in base-case year 4 and a two-year downturn in the bear case so that cyclicality is priced in the flows. 10-year horizon because capex and margins are still normalising at year 5. Terminal cap 16x owner FCF, below the house 20x default, for a half-cyclical industrial; at 8%/2% Gordon is 17x so the cap binds in base and bull.

equity_bridge.item: Equity instruments at fair value (Y1,853mn, FY2025 AR line 11867) + time deposits (Y2,667mn, line 9653)
equity_bridge.note: Matching-asset rule: these assets' income (Y3mn dividends, small deposit interest) sits below operating profit and is not in the flows, so the assets go in the bridge at fair value. Worth ~Y10/share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2026-28 average revenue growth (9.9% guided FY2026, 7%, 4%), a haircut to the E-Plan 2028 path (~Y1.2tn by FY2028 = 7.8% CAGR) and well below the 11.4% equity 5yr CAGR, which was earned over a semicap upcycle from a 2020 trough.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 26.5% is >30% above the equity (11.4%) and revenue (12.8%) CAGRs: FY2020 is a JGAAP trough year (OP margin 6.5%) and FY2025 an IFRS peak (11.9%), so the EPS figure is margin expansion plus an accounting-regime change, not a sustainable growth rate. Not used.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs use FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), skipping the FY2017-9mo stub. The 5yr window straddles the JGAAP->IFRS switch at FY2021. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC) is Y32,849mn in FY2020, Y12,153mn in FY2022 and -Y53,192mn in FY2025, so both FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative endpoint); the FY2025 collapse is the capex spike plus a working-capital build, not an operating deterioration (EBITDA +16% YoY). SBC is 0.2% of revenue and does not move the series.

base.growth_note: FY2026 = Aug-2026 raised guidance Y1,053bn (+9.9%). FY2027 +7% on the record Y1,245bn FY2026 order book (+31% YoY). FY2028 +4% lands near Y1.14tn, short of the E-Plan ~Y1.2tn. FY2029 flat = a WFE digestion year after three years of AI-driven growth. Thereafter 3-4% fading to 2.5%: GDP-plus for the industrial base, mid-cycle for semicap.
base.margin_note: FY2025 EBITDA 15.5% (OP 11.9%, D&A 3.6%). FY2026 guidance OP 11.9% on Y125bn -> EBITDA ~15.7%. Mid-cycle 16.5% = OP ~12.6% after adding back the 0.72% lease charge; below the E-Plan 14.5% OP target, which the base case treats as a stretch. Year 4 dips 1pp in the digestion year.
base.capex_note: H1 FY2026 capex Y41.8bn -> ~8% of FY2026 revenue (E-Plan growth capex incl. Kumamoto/Fujisawa precision capacity and a chemical-recycling pilot). Normalises to 4.2%: FY2021-23 averaged 4.1% while growing 10%+/yr, and terminal D&A (ex-ROU) of 3.6% plus ~0.6% growth capex on 2.5% growth gives 4.2%.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer with receivables + inventory + contract assets well above payables and contract liabilities: growth consumes cash. -15% of the revenue change; the engine releases it automatically in a down year.
base.tax_note: 31.5% = 28.8% cash tax on OP + 2.6% NCI leakage; see inputs.nci_treatment.

bull.note: E-Plan 2028 delivered: revenue ~Y1.25tn by FY2028 (Precision Machinery 15%+ CAGR to a 20%+ OP margin), group OP ratio reaching the 14.5% target (EBITDA 18.5%) and holding, no WFE digestion year inside the horizon. Same capex path and WACC as base; the bull is a flows story, not a discount-rate story.

bear.note: FY2026 misses guidance (7% vs 9.9%) on Kumamoto supply-chain and Middle East Energy delays; FY2027-28 a classic WFE digestion (-5%, -6%) with Precision Machinery margins compressing on under-absorbed new capacity, Energy stuck near breakeven, China BS&I soft. Margins recover only to 14% EBITDA (OP ~10.5%, below FY2024-25). Capex is cut to maintenance (4%) from FY2028. Terminal growth 1.5%: Gordon at 8%/1.5% is 15.6x, so Gordon binds and the cap does not.

scenario_narratives.base: Ebara rides the FY2026 AI-driven WFE upcycle exactly as guided (revenue Y1,053bn, OP Y125bn), converts the record Y1,245bn order book into +7% FY2027 growth, then hits a one-year semicap digestion in FY2029 before settling at 3-4% growth. Group EBITDA margin drifts from 15.7% to a mid-cycle 16.5% (OP ~12.6%) -- credit for Precision Machinery mix and the S&S/O&M tail, but short of the 14.5% E-Plan OP target. The FY2025-26 capex surge (9.6% then 8% of revenue) normalises to 4.2% by FY2033, so owner FCF rebuilds from ~Y19bn in FY2026 to ~Y100bn by the terminal year. The axes that matter: WFE cycle timing, whether the new precision capacity earns its 25% segment-ROIC target, and Energy's recovery from its H1 FY2026 loss.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI capex supercycle runs through FY2028 without a digestion year: Precision Machinery compounds at 15%+ to a 20%+ OP margin as advanced-packaging CMP (PLP, EAPI) and sub-fab solutions (LA+, EVIS) win share, Energy recovers to its 12%+ margin on LNG/hydrogen compressors, and the S&S mix lifts the group to the 14.5% E-Plan OP ratio (18.5% EBITDA) by FY2029 and holds it. Revenue reaches ~Y1.25tn by FY2028 and ~Y1.6tn by FY2035. Capex, WACC and tax are identical to base: the bull is entirely about margins and growth sticking.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 comes in light as Kumamoto earthquake supply-chain effects and Middle East shipment delays bite in H2, then 2027-28 brings the digestion phase that follows every WFE boom (-5%, -6% group revenue) just as Y180bn of new precision capacity comes on line, compressing Precision Machinery margins; Energy stays near breakeven on Jeannette plant and geopolitics, China BS&I keeps shrinking. EBITDA troughs at 12% and only recovers to 14% (OP ~10.5%). Capex is slashed to maintenance from FY2028, which cushions FCF, but the terminal business is smaller and lower-margin than today's. Order-book cancellations, an export-control tightening on China-bound semicap tools, or a second JFTC action are the triggers.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: Ebara's incremental profit is now dominated by one cyclical end market at what management itself calls an 18%+ WFE growth year, a digestion phase within a 10-year horizon is the historical norm rather than a tail event, and FY2025-26 capex is being committed into that cycle. Bull down to 25%: it requires three independent things -- no WFE digestion through FY2028, the E-Plan 14.5% OP target actually reached (vs 11.9% guided for FY2026), and Energy's H1 FY2026 loss reversing -- and the base case already credits the raised FY2026 guidance in full. The ~45% share-price fall since August 2026 is noted but does not by itself change the operating odds.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is degenerate: SBC is 0.18% of revenue, so street IV exceeds house IV by only ~Y75/share (~3%). band_position is therefore not a meaningful regime reading -- treat it as n/a, as in an SBC-zero market. The price sits far above BOTH bases.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A half-cyclical Japanese industrial valued on owner FCF rebuilt from components, with the FY2025 capex spike and working-capital build treated as a trough in FCF rather than a run-rate. Cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the WACC. Leases are an operating cost (treatment B), NCI is a leakage rate on the flows, SBC is visible but immaterial, and the terminal multiple is capped at 16x owner FCF because a business whose highest-margin segment follows the WFE cycle should not be capitalised like a mature compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Semiconductor capex cycle: Precision Machinery is ~36% of revenue and ~50% of segment profit; a WFE downturn in FY2027-28 is the bear case and the single largest swing factor
Capex conversion: FY2025-26 capex of ~Y180bn must earn the targeted 25% segment ROIC; if it is capacity into a downturn, both FCF and margins disappoint together
Terminal FCF conversion: owner FCF is only ~45% of EBITDA at terminal (31.5% tax+NCI, capex above D&A, WC drag); each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly Y150/share
Energy segment: H1 FY2026 operating loss (Middle East, Jeannette plant, pension settlement); the base case assumes recovery to ~12% margin inside the group figure
FX: two-thirds of revenue is overseas; FY2026 plan assumes JPY145/USD, a stronger yen than FY2025's 149.6, so translation is a headwind if the yen strengthens further
Lease-liability split at 30 June 2026 is estimated (held at the FY2025 Y23.4bn); a Y5bn error is ~Y11/share
